items.s: Price (head) was back on the field for the second quarter of Sunday's game against the Colts, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports. Price was being evaluated by medical staff for a possible concussion, but he's been cleared to return to Sunday's contest. He'll see most of his playing time as a returner on special teams while operating in a rotational role on offense.

Price is being evaluated for a possible concussion and is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Colts. Price appeared to sustain the injury while catching a punt in the first quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game. Tai Felton could handle return duties on kickoffs and punts for as long as Price is out of the game.

items.h: Myles Price catches three passes in Week 5
items.s: Myles Price caught three of his four targets for 20 yards with one fumble lost in the Vikings' 23-13 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 5. Price has struggled to make an impact for head coach Kevin O'Connell, finishing with less than 30 receiving yards in each of his four contests. The pass-catcher can remain off rosters in all formats as the Vikings enter a Week 6 bye.

items.h: Myles Price sees one target in Week 2
items.s: Myles Price failed to catch his only target in the Vikings' 9-3 win over the Chicago Bears in Week 2. Price remains minimally involved in the Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, recording one target or less in each of the first two games. The wideout remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 3 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Price recorded five kickoff returns for 179 yards and one punt return for 13 yards in Sunday's 39-22 win over the Packers. The wide receiver also played on three offensive snaps but did not record a target. The second-year pro has yet to record a catch in his NFL career, but he seems to have a role as a returner.

items.h: Myles Price Making Push For Bigger Receiving Role?
items.s: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Myles Price logged an impressive preseason debut by catching all four of his targets for 51 yards and a touchdown on Saturday against the New York Giants. An undrafted free agent from Indiana, Price made the Vikings' 53-man roster last season and finished third in the NFL in kick return yards. The second-year pro is now competing with Tai Felton and Jeshaun Jones for a secondary receiving role in the Vikings' offense, and Price's team-best 28-yard reception and acrobatic touchdown catch on Saturday certainly helped his cause. Still firmly behind Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and Jauan Jennings, Price won't factor into most standard formats, but he's a…

Price passed his conditioning test and is good to go for training camp, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports. The top kickoff and punt returner for the Vikings suffered an ankle injury in late Week 17 of last season. After an offseason of healing, Price is all set to suit up for training camp to attempt to defend his spot as the team's top return specialist. Tai Felton is the 24-year-old's primary competition for the role.

Price (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Packers, Dane Mizutani of the St. Paul Pioneer Press reports. Price didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday and is now in line to miss his first game of the season Sunday. The undrafted rookie from Indiana had a solid year while operating as the Vikings' primary return man, tallying 1,479 kick-return yards (third-most in the NFL) and 298 punt-return yards across 16 games. In his absence, expect Ty Chandler to operate as the Vikings' top return specialist in Week 18.

Price (ankle) was a non-participant in practice Wednesday. Price hurt his ankle Christmas Day versus Detroit and hasn't recovered enough to practice. With that in mind, it's uncertain if he'll be able to play in the Vikings' season finale against Green Bay on Sunday. Price has had just a bit role on offense this season, but he's been working as Minnesota's primary kick- and punt-returner, so he'd have to be replaced in those capacities if he can't suit up Sunday.

Price (ankle) has been ruled out to return to Thursday's game against the Vikings. Price suffered an ankle injury during the opening kickoff of Thursday's divisional matchup and will not retake the field. His next opportunity to return to action will come Sunday, Jan. 4 versus the Packers in Week 18.

items.h: Price, who injured his ankle on the opening kickoff of Thursday's game against Detroit, is questionable to return, Andrew Kramer of the Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
items.s: With Price injured, Jalen Nailor is handling punt returns. Price collapsed while running back a kickoff and was untouched.

items.h: Price returned six kickoffs for 143 yards in Sunday's 34-26 win over the Cowboys.
items.s: Price also took the field for a play on offense, but the depth receiver has yet to touch the ball as anything but a return man through his first 14 NFL games. While ball security (four fumbles) has been somewhat of an issue for Price, he's provided a boost to the Minnesota special teams with an average of 26.0 yards per kickoff return and 9.9 yards per punt return.

items.h: Price returned five kickoffs for an average of 32.8 yards, including a 61-yard return, in Sunday's win at Detroit. He also had a 99-yard touchdown return called back due to a holding penalty. He had one punt return for…
items.s: Price's returns had a big impact on the victory, as it set up the Vikings with good field position early in the game. His 61-yard return was the team's longest since 2022, according to the Minnesota Star Tribune.

items.h: Price averaged 25.0 yards on two kickoff returns and 13.6 yards on five punt returns in Sunday's win over the Bengals.
items.s: Price rebounded after a disappointing Week 2 performance where he lost a fumble. Against the Bengals, he looked more like the above-average returner he proved to be in Week 1.

items.h: Price averaged just 22.5 yards on six kick returns and averaged 2.0 yards on three punt returns in Monday's loss to Atlanta. He also lost a fumble on a punt return.
items.s: Price looked like a potential star returner in Week 1 as he averaged 17 yards per punt return, but he looked like a cut candidate in Week 2 with underwhelming returns and a lost fumble.

items.h: Price averaged 17.0 yards on four punt returns and 24.5 yards on three kickoff returns in Monday's win at Chicago.
items.s: Price is Minnesota's punt returner and a primary kickoff returner along with Ty Chandler. He made a significant impact in Monday's game, and it looks like the rookie could be a star return man.

items.h: Price will begin the season as Minnesota's punt returner and reserve wide receiver, the Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
items.s: Price was an undrafted free agent from Indiana who likely made the team because of Rondale Moore's season-ending knee injury. He's unlikely to get many snaps on offense, however.

items.h: Price signed with the Vikings as an undrafted free agent Friday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
items.s: Price spent the first four years of his collegiate career at Texas Tech before transferring to Indiana in 2024. The 5-foot-9 wideout was one of Indiana's top playmakers during the team's College Football Playoff run last season, catching 38 passes for 466 yards and three touchdowns. He also added seven carries for 63 yards and one rushing touchdown. While Price is likely an extra body for offseason activities, he could earn a spot on the Vikings' practice squad if he impresses this summer.
